$$r\colon\mathscr{L}(L)=\mathscr{L}(K+\mathbf{y}_{\mathbf{t}(\alpha)})\cong\mathscr{L}(K)+\mathscr{L}(\mathbf{y}_{\mathbf{t}(\alpha)})\rightarrow E_{p}$$is obtained by copairing $\ell$ and the bottom composite
in~\eqref{eq:cellpremise}.
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@For each rigid rule
\begin{equation*}\frac{(k_{i}\colon s_{v}^{d^{\mathbf{p}}_{o,i}}\rightarrow\mathbf{p})_{i\in\{1,\ldots,N^{\mathbf{p}}_{o}\}}=K_{0}\xrightarrow{e_{1}\mathrel{\alpha_{1}}k_{1}}K_{1}\rightarrow\ldots\rightarrow K_{n-1}\xrightarrow{e_{n}\mathrel{\alpha_{n}}k_{n}}K_{n}}{o(k_{1},\ldots,k_{N_{o}^{\mathbf{p}}})\Downarrow k^{\prime\prime}}~\hbox to0.0pt{,\hss}\end{equation*}say $r$, we define
\begin{equation}\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}(X)(\Downarrow)=[E_{p_{1}},X]\times_{[\mathscr{L}(K_{1}),X]}\ldots\times_{[\mathscr{L}(K_{p-1}),X]}[E_{p_{n}},X]\hbox to0.0pt{,\hss}\end{equation}where for all $i\in n$, $\mathscr{L}(K_{i-1})\xrightarrow{s_{i}}E_{p_{i}}\xleftarrow{t_{i}}\mathscr{L}(K_{i})$
denotes the cospan induced by the $i$th premise, with
$\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}(X)(\Downarrow^{+}_{o^{\prime},i})=\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}(X)(\Downarrow^{-}_{o^{\prime},j})=\emptyset$ for all
$o^{\prime}\in O_{\mathbf{v}}$, $i\in N^{+}_{o^{\prime}}$, $j\in N^{-}_{o^{\prime}}$, and again with the morphism
$\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}(X)\rightarrow\Sigma_{0}^{B}(X)\mathbf{s}\times X\mathbf{t}$ mapping any compatible tuple
$(\rho_{1},\ldots,\rho_{n})\in\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}(X)(\Downarrow)$ to $(in_{o}(a),b)$,
where $a\in\prod_{i\in N^{\mathbf{p}}_{o}}X((d^{\mathbf{p}}_{o,i})_{\mathbf{p}})$ corresponds by Yoneda and adjunction to the morphism
$$\mathscr{L}(K_{0})\xrightarrow{s_{1}}E_{1}\xrightarrow{\rho_{1}}X,$$and
$b\in X(0_{v})$ corresponds to
$$\mathscr{L}(\mathbf{y}_{0_{\mathbf{v}}})\xrightarrow{\mathscr{L}(in_{2})}\mathscr{L}(K_{n})\xrightarrow{t_{n}}E_{n}\xrightarrow{\rho_{n}}X.$$\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@We let $(\Sigma_{1}^{B,D})^{F}=\sum_{o\in O_{\mathbf{v}}}\Sigma_{1,o}^{F}+\sum_{r}\Sigma_{1,r}^{F}$,
with morphism to $\Sigma_{0}^{B}(-)\mathbf{s}\times(-)\mathbf{t}$ given by cotupling.
\end{itemize}\par By construction, we have:
\begin{prop}The transition $\Sigma_{0}^{B}$-monoid generated by the dynamic signature
$\Sigma_{1}^{B,D}$ is isomorphic to the rigid transition system $R(B,D)$.
\end{prop}Furthermore,
we observe:
\begin{lem}The induced functor $(\Sigma_{1}^{B,D})^{\mathbf{s}}$ is cellular.
\end{lem}\begin{proof}The functor is familial by construction. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:cellularenough}\ref{item:explicit} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:cellscof}, it suffices to show that for
any rule $r$ whose conclusion is a transition of type $\alpha$, the
boundary arity $$E(s_{\alpha}\upharpoonright r)\colon E(\mathbf{s}(\alpha),r\cdot s_{\alpha})\rightarrow E(\alpha,r)$$is a
relative cell complex. The arity of each canonical
rule~\eqref{rules:canonical} is clearly a coproduct of
generating cofibrations. The arities of canonical
rules~\eqref{rules:new}
are identities, hence trivially
relative cell complexes. For any other rule $r$,
by~\eqref{eq:Howearity} the arity is the left-hand leg of cospan
obtained by composing all $K_{i-1}\rightarrow E_{i}\leftarrow K_{i}$, which is thus by
construction a composite of pushouts of generating cofibrations,
hence a relative cell complex.
\end{proof}We at last obtain:
\begin{thm}For any Howe binding signature $B$ and dynamic signature $D$,
the open extension of applicative bisimilarity on the generated
transition system is a congruence.
\end{thm}\begin{proof}The open extension of applicative bisimilarity for $(B,D)$
coincides with substitution-closed bisimilarity for $R(B,D)$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:adequacy}, which further coincides with
substitution-closed for the transition system generated by
$\Sigma_{1}^{B,D}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:furtheradequacy}. Finally,
the latter is a congruence by Lemmas~\ref{lem:characfib}
and~\ref{lem:howecellular}, and Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
\end{proof}\par\par\par\@@numbered@section{section}{toc}{Congruence of substitution-closed bisimilarity}
In this section, we elaborate on the proof sketch of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} given in~\lx@sectionsign\ref{s:substclosedbisim}. The
overall structure remains the same, and the final part of the proof
sketch is complete, so we mainly elaborate on
items~\ref{item:wowo}--\ref{item:sym}.
\par\par\@@numbered@section{subsection}{toc}{Preliminaries on spans}
In this section, we fix a locally finitely presentable category $\mathscr{C}$,
recall some known tools about spans, and develop a few new ones,
including categorified notions of reflexivity, transitivity, symmetry,
and transitive closure. As announced in~\lx@sectionsign\ref{ss:notation}, we freely
switch from spans $X\leftarrow S\rightarrow Y$ to their pairings $S\rightarrow X\times Y$ in
$\mathscr{C}/X\times Y$. Furthermore,
\defi
Given any spans $R\xrightarrow{\langle p_{1},p_{2}\rangle}X\times Y$ and $S\xrightarrow{\langle q_{1},q_{2}\rangle}Y\times Z$,
their \emph{span}, or \emph{sequential}, composition, denoted by
${R;S}\rightarrow X\times Z$, is the (or, rather, some global choice of) following
span obtained by pullback.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}
\end{center}from the diagonal to $S$ in $\mathscr{C}/X^{2}$. It is \emph{transitive} if there
is a morphism $S;S\rightarrow S$ in $\mathscr{C}/X^{2}$. Finally, it is \emph{symmetric}
if there is a morphism $S^{\dagger}\rightarrow S$, where $(-)^{\dagger}$ denotes the functor
swapping projections, i.e., mapping any $R\xrightarrow{\langle p_{1},p_{2}\rangle}X^{2}$ to
$R\xrightarrow{\langle p_{2},p_{1}\rangle}X^{2}$.
\par For potentially non-reflexive spans, we will use the following
reflexive transitive closure.
\defi
The \emph{reflexive transitive closure} $S^{*}$ of any span $S\rightarrow X^{2}$
is the coproduct $\sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}}S^{{;}n}$, or for short $\sum_{n\in\mathbb{N}}S^{n}$
when the context is clear, where $S^{{;}n}$ denotes iterated span
composition of $S$ with itself, inductively defined by
$S^{{;}0}=X$ and $S^{{;}n+1}=S^{{;}n};S$.
\par At some point, we will also use a more ``relational'' notion of
transitive closure, which we now introduce.
\defi
Given a span $S\rightarrow X^{2}$, we denote by $\overline{S}$ the relation on
$X$ induced by the image factorisation of $S\rightarrow X\times X$.
\defi
The \emph{relational transitive closure} $S^{\overline{+}}$ of a span
$S$ on $X$ is the union $\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{S^{{;}n}}$.
\begin{rem}Unions of relations exist by Proposition~\ref{prop:union}, as we
have assumed the ambient category $\mathscr{C}$ to be locally finitely
presentable.
\end{rem}\par We immediately observe the following.
\begin{lem}For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, spans $S\rightarrow X^{2}$ and $R\rightarrow X^{2}$, and families
$(S_{i}\rightarrow X^{2})_{i\in I}$ of relations spans, we have
\begin{enumerate}\enumerate@item@$\overline{S^{\dagger}}\cong\overline{S}^{\dagger}$,
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\enumerate@item@$(R;S)^{\dagger}\cong S^{\dagger};R^{\dagger}$, hence
$(S^{\dagger})^{{;}n}\cong(S^{{;}n})^{\dagger}$, and
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\enumerate@item@$\bigcup_{i\in I}S_{i}^{\dagger}\cong(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_{i})^{\dagger}$.
\end{enumerate}\end{lem}\begin{proof}Let $\sigma:=\langle\pi_{2},\pi_{1}\rangle\colon X^{2}\rightarrow X^{2}$.
\begin{itemize}\itemize@item@For~\eqref{item:symrel}, by definition each side of the
isomorphism corresponds to one side of the exterior of the
following commuting pentagon.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}
\end{center}But, $\sigma$ being an isomorphism, both sides are strong epi-mono
factorisations of the morphism $\langle\pi_{2},\pi_{1}\rangle\colon S\rightarrow X^{2}$, hence are isomorphic.
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@The first point of~\eqref{item:symseq} is clear. For the
second one, we proceed by induction. The base case is
trivial, and assuming $(S^{\dagger})^{{;}n}\cong(S^{{;}n})^{\dagger}$, we have
$$(S^{\dagger})^{{;}n+1}\cong(S^{\dagger})^{{;}n};S^{\dagger}\cong(S^{{;}n})^{\dagger};S^{\dagger}\cong(S;S^{{;}n})^{\dagger}\cong(S^{{;}n+1})^{\dagger}\hbox to0.0pt{,\hss}$$hence the result.
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@For~\eqref{item:symU} we have
$\bigcup_{i\in I}S_{i}^{\dagger}=\overline{\sum_{i\in I}S_{i}^{\dagger}}$ and
$(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_{i})^{\dagger}=\overline{(\sum_{i\in I}S_{i})}^{\dagger}\cong\overline{(\sum_{i\in I}S_{i})^{\dagger}}$ by~\eqref{item:symrel}, so it
suffices to show $\sum_{i\in I}S_{i}^{\dagger}\cong(\sum_{i\in I}S_{i})^{\dagger}$. But,
letting $b_{i}\colon S_{i}\rightarrow X^{2}$ denote each projection, the former is
(shorthand for) the morphism $[\sigma\circ b_{i}]_{i}\colon\sum_{i}S_{i}\rightarrow X^{2}$, and the
latter is $\sigma\circ[b_{i}]_{i}$, which are in fact equal.
\end{itemize}\end{proof}\begin{cor}For all spans $S\rightarrow X^{2}$, we have
$S^{\dagger\overline{+}}\cong S^{\overline{+}\dagger}$.
\end{cor}\begin{proof}We have $S^{\dagger\overline{+}}=\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{(S^{\dagger})^{{;}n}}\cong(\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{S^{{;}n}})^{\dagger}\cong S^{\overline{+}\dagger}$, by the lemma.
\end{proof}The following lemma will later be used to exploit preservation of
sifted colimits by $\Sigma_{0}$.
\begin{lem}If $S$ is a reflexive span on $X$, then $S^{\overline{+}}$ is the (filtered) colimit of the chain
$$X\rightarrow\overline{S}\cong\overline{S;X}\rightarrow\overline{S;S}\cong\overline{S;S;X}\rightarrow\overline{S;S;S}\rightarrow{\ldots}$$\end{lem}\begin{proof}Consider a colimiting cone for the given diagram, say to
$C\in\mathscr{C}$. Because the forgetful functor $\mathscr{C}/X^{2}\rightarrow\mathscr{C}$ creates
colimits, it is in fact a colimiting cocone in $\mathscr{C}/X^{2}$. Now, the
diagram consists of monic morphisms, hence
by~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Adamek}{}{}, Proposition~1.62(i)]}, so does the colimiting
cocone. Furthermore, by~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Adamek}{}{}, Proposition~1.62(ii)]}, the
mediating morphism $C\rightarrow X^{2}$ is again monic. The cocone thus
lifts to the category $\mathbf{R}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{l}(X)$ of (binary) relations over
$X$. Because the forgetful functor $\mathbf{R}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{l}(X)\rightarrow\mathscr{C}/X^{2}$ is fully
faithful, the cocone remains colimiting in $\mathbf{R}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{l}(X)$. Finally,
$\mathbf{R}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{l}(X)$ is a preorder category, so the colimit of the
considered, directed diagram is equally a colimit of the
underlying discrete diagram, which is $S^{\overline{+}}$ by
definition.
\end{proof}\par The next result will be useful to show that the relational
transitive closure of the Howe closure of substitution-closed
bisimilarity is symmetric on states.
\par\begin{lem}For any reflexive span $R\rightarrow X^{2}$, $R^{\overline{+}}$ is symmetric
if there exists a span morphism $R\rightarrow R^{\overline{+}\dagger}$.
\end{lem}\begin{proof}Given a morphism $j\colon R\rightarrow R^{\overline{+}\dagger}$, we consider the
composite
$$R^{\overline{+}}=\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{R^{;n}}\rightarrow\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{(R^{\overline{+}\dagger})^{;n}}\cong\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{((R^{\overline{+}})^{;n})^{\dagger}}\rightarrow\bigcup_{n>0}\overline{R^{\overline{+}\dagger}}\cong\bigcup_{n>0}{R^{\overline{+}\dagger}}\cong R^{\overline{+}\dagger},$$where the first morphism is obtained from $j$, and the second one
is obtained from morphisms $(R^{\overline{+}})^{;n}\rightarrow R^{\overline{+}}$.
\end{proof}\par\par\par\@@numbered@section{subsection}{toc}{Howe closure on states}
We fix an operational semantics signature $(\Sigma_{0},\Sigma_{1})$ on a Howe context
$\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t}\colon\mathbb{C}_{1}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}_{0}$, and recall
\begin{itemize}\itemize@item@from Notation~\ref{not:Z0} that $\mathbf{Z}_{0}$
denotes the initial $\Sigma_{0}$-monoid,
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@from Theorem~\ref{thm:Z} that $\mathbf{Z}$ denotes the initial vertical
$\check{\Sigma}_{1}$-algebra (hence in particular that $\mathscr{D}(\mathbf{Z})=\mathbf{Z}_{0}$), and
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@from Notation~\ref{not:simtens} that $\sim^{\otimes}$ denotes
substitution-closed bisimilarity on $\mathbf{Z}$ (hence in particular that
$\mathscr{D}(\sim^{\otimes})={\sim^{\otimes}_{0}}$ is its state part).
\end{itemize}\defi Let $\Sigma_{0}^{H}\colon\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ map any span $X\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ to
$$\Sigma_{0}(X)+(X;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes}})\rightarrow\Sigma_{0}(\mathbf{Z}_{0})^{2}+\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}\hbox to0.0pt{.\hss}$$\par This functor $\Sigma_{0}^{H}$ is clearly inspired from the standard Howe closure.
We now want to prove that it is pointed strong, which requires us to
equip $\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ with monoidal structure. But $\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ is a monoid, and it
is well-known~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Weber:genmorph}{}{}, \lx@sectionsign 2]} that any slice of a monoidal
category over any monoid $M$ is again monoidal. The tensor of $X\rightarrow M$
and $Y\rightarrow M$ is simply $X\otimes Y\rightarrow M\otimes M\rightarrow M$, and the unit is $I\rightarrow M$. We
may thus state the following result.
\begin{prop}The functor $\Sigma_{0}^{H}$ is pointed strong.
\end{prop}\par For proving this, we first need the following.
\begin{lem}For any monoid $X$ in any monoidal category $\mathscr{C}$ with finite limits, there is a natural transformation with components
$\delta_{U,V,W}\colon(U;V)\otimes W\rightarrow U\otimes W;V\otimes X$ in $\mathscr{C}/X^{2}$.
\end{lem}\begin{proof}Let $m\colon X\otimes X\rightarrow X$ denote multiplication.
By tensoring the defining pullback of $U;V$ with $W$ we obtain the

making all faces commute, which gives our candidate $\delta_{U,V,W}$.
Naturality follows by universal property of pullback.
\end{proof}\par\par\par\begin{proof}Because the tensor preserves all colimits on the left, pointed
strong endofunctors are closed under coproducts, so it suffices to
show that both terms of the sum are pointed strong. The first one
inherits the pointed strength of $\Sigma_{0}$, while the pointed strength of
${-};{\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}$ follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:distrib} and
substitution-closedness of ${\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}$, like so:
$(U;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes}})\otimes V\rightarrow(U\otimes V);({\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}\otimes\mathbf{Z}_{0})\rightarrow(U\otimes V);{\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}\hbox to0.0pt{.\hss}$
\end{proof}\par Presheaf categories being well-known to be closed under the slice
construction, we have the following.
\begin{lem}The category $\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ is a presheaf category.
\end{lem}This allows us to deduce the following.
\begin{prop}The endofunctor $\Sigma_{0}^{H}$ is finitary.
\end{prop}\begin{proof}By commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits in presheaf
categories.
\end{proof}\par\par\par By Proposition~\ref{prop:SoHptstr}, Lemma~\ref{lem:CZpresheaf}, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:SoHfinitary}, the following is legitimate.
\defi
Let ${H_{0}}=\mathbf{Z}_{\Sigma_{0}^{H}}$ denote the initial $\Sigma_{0}^{H}$-monoid. We denote by
$\pi_{1},\pi_{2}\colon H_{0}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}$ the left and right projections.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:ptstrgeneral}, we also get the following for free.
\begin{prop}The object ${H_{0}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ is an initial algebra for the
endofunctor $\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ mapping any $X\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ to
$I+\Sigma_{0}^{H}(X)\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$.
\end{prop}\par\begin{prop}The underlying object ${H_{0}}$ is a $\Sigma_{0}$-monoid.
\end{prop}\begin{proof}Directly follows from the $\Sigma_{0}^{H}$-monoid structure.
\end{proof}\par Next, we exhibit an alternative characterisation of ${H_{0}}$, which relies
on the following result.
\begin{lem}Consider finitary endofunctors $F$ and $G$ on a cocomplete category
$\mathbf{C}$, and let $G^{\star}(A)\cong\mu S.(A+G(S))$ denote the `free $G$-algebra'
monad~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Reiterman}{}{}, Theorem~2.1]}. Then we have
$\mu S.(F(S)+G(S))\cong\mu S.G^{\star}(F(S))$.
\end{lem}\begin{proof}Indeed, we have
\begin{center}$\begin{array}[b]{rcl}\mu S.G^{\star}(F(S))&\cong&\mu S.\mu U.(F(S)+G(U))\\
&\cong&\mu S.(F(S)+G(S))\hbox to0.0pt{,\hss}\end{array}$
\end{center}by the Diagonal rule~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{DBLP:conf/ctcs/BackhouseBGW95}{}{}, Theorem~16]}.
\end{proof}\par\begin{prop}The object ${H_{0}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ is an initial algebra for the
endofunctor $$\Sigma_{0}^{H}{}^{\prime}\colon\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$$mapping any $X\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ to
$I;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}}+\Sigma_{0}(X);{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$.
\end{prop}\begin{proof}Let $F(S)=I+\Sigma_{0}(S)$ and $G(S)=S;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}$. We observe that $G$
preserves coproducts (because pullback along the first projection
${\sim_{0}^{\otimes}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}$, as a left adjoint, preserves colimits), so that
$G^{\star}(U)\cong\sum_{n}G^{n}(U)$. By commutation of coproducts with $U;{-}$, we
thus have
$$G^{\star}(U)\cong\sum_{n}G^{n}(U)\cong\sum_{n}U;(\sim_{0}^{\otimes})^{n}\cong U;\sum_{n}(\sim_{0}^{\otimes})^{n}=U;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}}\hbox to0.0pt{.\hss}$$Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:muFplusG}, we get
$G^{\star}(F(S))\cong(I+\Sigma_{0}(S));{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}}\cong(I;{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}})+(\Sigma_{0}(S);{\sim_{0}^{\otimes*}})$, as desired.
\end{proof}\par\par\@@numbered@section{subsection}{toc}{Double categorical notation}
Our next goal is to define the Howe closure on transitions. For this,
we appeal to Morton's \emph{double bicategories}~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Morton}{}{}]}. They
are a refinement of double categories, in which both the horizontal
and vertical categories are bicategories. We rely in particular on his
Theorem~4.1.3, which (when dualised) states that for any category $\mathscr{C}$
with pullbacks, there is a double bicategory $\mathit{2Sp}(\mathscr{C})$:
\begin{itemize}\itemize@item@objects are objects of $\mathscr{C}$,
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@both the vertical and horizontal bicategories are $\mathit{Span}(\mathscr{C})$,
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@cells, called \emph{double spans}, are precisely commuting
diagrams of the following form.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}} \end{center}\end{itemize}\par Cells of the form~\eqref{eq:doublecell} live in $\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}})$, hence
may be composed horizontally. Relevant examples of vertical
composition will be obtained by embedding cells of the
form~\eqref{eq:cell0} along $\Delta_{\mathbf{s}}$ (resp.\ $\Delta_{\mathbf{t}}$), and
vertically composing with cells of the form~\eqref{eq:doublecell} in
$\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}})$. This yields a top (resp.\ bottom) action of
$\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}})$, which we both denote by mere pasting.
\par\begin{lem}Given a composable pasting diagram made of cells of both types,
any two parsings agree up to isomorphism.
\end{lem}\begin{proof}By interchange of limits.
\end{proof}\par Let us end this subsection by generalising simulations to
$\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}})$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:sim:wpbk}, the span
denoted by a cell~(\ref{eq:doublecell}, right) in $\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}})$ is
a simulation iff the top left square in the corresponding
diagram~(\ref{eq:doublecell}, left) is a pointwise weak pullback.
Abstracting over this:
\defi
A cell in any double bicategory of the form $\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}})$ is a
\emph{simulation} iff its top left square is a pointwise weak
pullback.
\begin{prop}Simulations are closed under horizontal and vertical composition
in any double bicategory of the form $\mathit{2Sp}(\widehat{\mathbb{C}})$.
\end{prop}In order to prove this, we need the following weak analogues of the
pullback lemma.
\nota
We denote
weak pullbacks (in any category) by dashed corners.

delineate an ambient category $\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$. The idea is that objects of
this category should be transition systems $S\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}^{2}$ over $\mathbf{Z}^{2}$ whose
image under the projection $\mathbf{C}/\mathbf{Z}^{2}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{0}}/\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$ is precisely $H_{0}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}^{2}$.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\end{equation}Equivalently, they are morphisms over the limit, so that we may define
$\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ as a slice category by merely stating the
following.
\defi
Let $R^{\partial H}$ denote the limit of the outer part of~\eqref{eq:doublebicat}.
\defi
$\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the category of cones over the
outer part of~\eqref{eq:doublebicat}, or equivalently,
it is the slice category $\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}}/R^{\partial H}$.
\par Furthermore, we denote by $\mathscr{U}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\colon\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\rightarrow\mathbf{C}/\mathbf{Z}^{2}$ the forgetful
functor.
\begin{prop}The initial object in $\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the span $\mathbf{Z}\leftarrow{H_{0}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}$, i.e., the
one with $S_{1}=0$.
\end{prop}\par\defi Let $\Sigma_{1}^{H}\colon\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\rightarrow\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ map any object $\mathbf{Z}\leftarrow S\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}$ to the coproduct of
the following two pastings.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}\end{equation}\par\begin{prop}The functor $\Sigma_{1}^{H}\colon\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\rightarrow\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ is finitary.
\end{prop}\begin{proof}The forgetful functor $\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\cong\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}}/R^{\partial H}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}}$ creates colimits,
so it suffices to show that the composite
$\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\xrightarrow{\Sigma_{1}^{H}}\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}\rightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}}$ is finitary. This functor maps any
$S$ to $\Sigma_{1}^{F}(S)+{S_{1};{\sim_{1}}^{\otimes}}$, hence is finitary because
$\Sigma_{1}^{F}$ is and ${-};\sim_{1}^{\otimes}$ is cocontinuous.
\end{proof}\par The last result legitimates the following definition.
\defi
Let $H_{\mathbf{Z}}$ denote the initial $\Sigma_{1}^{H}$-algebra. We call
$H:=\mathscr{U}^{H}_{\mathbf{Z}}(H_{\mathbf{Z}})\in\mathbf{C}/\mathbf{Z}^{2}$ the \emph{Howe closure} of
substitution-closed bisimilarity.
\par We readily can prove the following. See \ref{restatable:simintowow}
\begin{proof}By construction, the underlying object of $H$ is in particular a
$\check{\Sigma}_{1}$-algebra, so by initiality we obtain a unique span
morphism $\mathbf{Z}\rightarrow{H}$ --- in other words $H$ is reflexive.
Furthermore, again by construction, ${H}$ is an algebra for the
endofunctor ${-};{\sim^{\otimes}}$ on $\mathbf{C}/\mathbf{Z}^{2}$. We thus may form the composite
${\sim^{\otimes}}\cong\mathbf{Z};{\sim^{\otimes}}\rightarrow{H};{\sim^{\otimes}}\rightarrow{H}$.
\end{proof}\par\par\par\@@numbered@section{subsection}{toc}{Alternative characterisations of the Howe closure}
In this section, we exhibit a few alternative characterisations of the
Howe closure on transitions. The definition in the previous section
is convenient for proving that the transitive closure is symmetric,
while our final alternative characterisation will enable a conceptual
proof of the simulation property.

\end{cor}\begin{proof}This follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:commute-free-monads} with $F=U$, $G=W$, $K$ as $RK$ where
$R$ is the right adjoint of $J$,
by considering the mate
$\alpha^{\prime}:UR\rightarrow RV$ of $\alpha:JU\rightarrow VJ$,
defined as
$UR\xrightarrow{\eta UR}RJUR\xrightarrow{R\alpha R}RVJR\xrightarrow{RV\varepsilon}RV$,
(where $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ denote the unit and the counit of the adjunction $J\dashv R$)
and composing it with $\beta$ to get a natural
transformation $URK\rightarrow RKW$.

\lxSVG@closescope {{
{}{}{}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}$$To this end, we are going to organise $\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{H}$ as a comma category on which $M$
acts, so as to apply Corollary~\ref{cor:commute-free-mon-adj}.
Let $\mathscr{A}$ denote the category of objects $S_{1}$ equipped with a span $\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1}$ and $\mathscr{B}$ denote the product category $\mathscr{B}_{\mathbf{s}}\times\mathscr{B}_{\mathbf{t}}$,
where $\mathscr{B}_{\sigma}$ is the category of
objects $S_{1}$ equipped with a span $\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma$.
\par Let $J:\mathscr{A}\rightarrow\mathscr{B}$ denote the functor mapping $\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1}$ to
$(\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{s}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{s},\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{t}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{t})$, by postcomposing with the relevant morphisms.
As the forgetful functor from a category of spans creates colimits, $J$ is
cocontinuous and thus has a right adjoint by~\cite[cite]{[\@@bibref{}{Adamek}{}{}, Theorem~1.66]}, since its domain is a
locally presentable category.
Let $K:1\rightarrow\mathscr{B}$ be the functor selecting the pair $(\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{s}\leftarrow H_{0}\mathbf{s}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{s},\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{t}\leftarrow H_{0}\mathbf{t}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\mathbf{t})$.
Now, it is straightforward to check that $\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{H}$ is isomorphic to the comma category $J/K$.
\par Next, we reconstruct $M$ as acting on $J/K$ through this isomorphism in order to fit the setting
of Corollary~\ref{cor:commute-free-mon-adj}.
\par Let
\begin{itemize}\itemize@item@$U:\mathscr{A}\rightarrow\mathscr{A}$ denote the functor mapping $\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1}$ to $\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow S_{1}\leftarrow S_{1};\sim^{\otimes}_{1}\rightarrow\sim^{\otimes}_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1}$;
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@$V:\mathscr{B}\rightarrow\mathscr{B}$ denote the functor $V_{\mathbf{s}}\times V_{\mathbf{t}}$, where $V_{\sigma}:\mathscr{B}_{\sigma}\rightarrow\mathscr{B}_{\sigma}$
maps $\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma$
to $\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma\leftarrow S_{1};\sim^{\otimes}_{0}\sigma\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{0}\sigma$;
\par\vskip 4.0pt\vskip 4.0pt plus 2.0pt minus 1.0pt\itemize@item@$W:1\rightarrow 1$ denote the identity endofunctor.
\end{itemize}Now we apply Corollary~\ref{cor:commute-free-mon-adj} with suitable
$\alpha:JU\rightarrow VJ$ and $\beta:WK\rightarrow KW$ so that $M$ corresponds to our endofunctor
through the isomorphism $\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{Z}}^{H}\cong J/K$.
Since $U^{\star}(\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow S_{1}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1})=(\mathbf{Z}_{1}\leftarrow{S_{1};{\sim^{\otimes*}_{1}}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{1})$, the only thing to check
is that the proposed definition for $M^{\star}(S_{1})$ indeed defines a $M$-algebra,
and that $S_{1}\rightarrow U^{\star}(S_{1})$ induces a morphism $S_{1}\rightarrow M^{\star}(S_{1})$, which is straightforward.
\end{proof}\par Letusnowturntoourfinalcharacterisationof$H$,whichreliesonthefollowingcategory,whichisarelaxationof$\mathbf{C}^H_\mathbf{Z}$,inwhichtheleft-handobjectin~\eqref{eq:doublebicat}isonlyforcedtocoincidewith$\mathbf{Z}$on$\widehat{\mathbb{C}_0}$.\defi Let$\mathbf{C}^{H}_{\mathit{lax}}$denotethecategorywhoseobjectsconsistofobjects$X_{1}$and$S_{1}$in$\widehat{\mathbb{C}_{1}}$,equippedwithdashedarrowsmakingthefollowingdiagramcommute.\begin{equation}\hbox to115.37pt{\vbox to73.85pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 57.68198pt\lower-36.92297pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@closescope \hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {}{}{{}}\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\hbox{\hbox{{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {{}{}{{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}{{}}}{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}}{{}{}{{
